/// Tracker-agnostic ADO ticket-operation tools (dm.ai #661/#663 parity):
/// definitions and executor handlers. Names, params, aliases and
/// descriptions mirror the Java `@MCPTool` annotations.
part of 'ado_tools.dart';

/// Id param with the Java `key` alias.
ToolParam _workItemId() => _idParam('The work item ID');

ToolParam _req(String name, String description,
        {List<String> aliases = const [], String type = 'string'}) =>
    ToolParam(
      name: name,
      description: description,
      aliases: aliases,
      type: type,
    );

ToolDefinition _opTool(
  String name,
  String description,
  List<ToolParam> params, {
  List<String> aliases = const [],
}) =>
    ToolDefinition(
      name: name,
      aliases: aliases,
      description: description,
      integration: 'ado',
      category: 'work_item_management',
      params: params,
    );

/// `ado_create_work_item` — Java `createWorkItemWithFieldsJson`.
ToolDefinition _createWorkItemTool() => _opTool(
      'ado_create_work_item',
      'Create a new work item in Azure DevOps',
      [
        _req('project', 'The project name'),
        _req('workItemType', 'The work item type (Bug, Task, User Story, etc.)',
            aliases: ['issueType', 'type']),
        _req('title', 'The work item title', aliases: ['summary']),
        ToolParam(
          name: 'description',
          description: 'The work item description (HTML)',
          required: false,
        ),
        ToolParam(
          name: 'fieldsJson',
          description: 'Additional fields as JSON object (e.g., '
              '{"Microsoft.VSTS.Common.Priority": 1})',
          required: false,
          type: 'object',
        ),
        ToolParam(
          name: 'parentId',
          description: 'Optional parent work item ID: the new item is '
              'created as its child (Hierarchy link)',
          required: false,
          aliases: ['parentKey'],
        ),
      ],
      aliases: ['tracker_create_ticket'],
    );

/// Ticket-operation tools added for dm.ai #661.
List<ToolDefinition> _ticketOpTools() => [
      _opTool('ado_move_to_state', 'Move a work item to a specific state', [
        _workItemId(),
        _req('state', 'The target state name', aliases: ['statusName']),
      ], aliases: [
        'tracker_move_to_status'
      ]),
      _opTool('ado_assign_work_item', 'Assign a work item to a user', [
        _workItemId(),
        _req('userEmail', 'The user email or display name',
            aliases: ['accountId']),
      ], aliases: [
        'tracker_assign_ticket',
        'tracker_assign'
      ]),
      _opTool(
          'ado_update_description', 'Update the description of a work item', [
        _workItemId(),
        _req('description', 'The new description (HTML format)'),
      ],
          aliases: [
            'tracker_update_description'
          ]),
      _opTool(
        'ado_update_tags',
        'Update the tags of a work item (semicolon-separated string)',
        [
          _workItemId(),
          _req(
              'tags',
              "Tags as semicolon-separated string (e.g., "
                  "'tag1;tag2;tag3')"),
        ],
      ),
      ..._ticketFieldTools(),
      ..._ticketLinkTools(),
    ];

/// Field-level tools: update-field, set-priority, get-field-code.
List<ToolDefinition> _ticketFieldTools() => [
      _opTool(
          'ado_update_field',
          'Update any field of a work item. The field may be a reference '
              'name (System.Title, Custom.SolutionDesign) or a common human '
              'name (summary, title, description, priority, tags, state, '
              'assignedTo, storyPoints), which is mapped to its reference '
              'name. Unknown names are passed through unchanged.',
          [
            _workItemId(),
            _req('field', 'Field reference name or common name'),
            _req('value', 'The new value'),
          ],
          aliases: [
            'tracker_update_field'
          ]),
      _opTool(
          'ado_set_priority',
          'Set the priority of a work item. Accepts the ADO numbers 1-4 or '
              'Jira-style names (Blocker/Highest/Critical=1, High/Major=2, '
              'Medium/Normal=3, Low/Minor/Lowest/Trivial=4).',
          [
            _workItemId(),
            _req('priority', 'Priority number 1-4 or a priority name'),
          ],
          aliases: [
            'tracker_set_priority'
          ]),
      _opTool(
          'ado_get_field_code',
          'Resolve a human-readable field name to its reference name for the '
              "project (the analogue of jira_get_field_custom_code). Returns "
              "e.g. 'Custom.SolutionDesign' or 'System.Title'; returns null "
              'when no field with that name exists.',
          [
            ToolParam(
              name: 'project',
              description: 'The project name (defaults to the configured '
                  'project)',
              required: false,
            ),
            _req(
                'fieldName',
                "The human-readable field name (e.g. 'Solution Design') or "

typedef _AdoHandler = Future<dynamic> Function(Map<String, dynamic>);

String _s(Map<String, dynamic> a, String key, [String? alt]) =>
    '${a[key] ?? (alt == null ? '' : a[alt]) ?? ''}';

/// Tracker-agnostic ADO ticket-operation tools (dm.ai #661/#663 parity):
/// definitions and executor handlers. Names, params, aliases and

part of 'ado_tools.dart';

/// Id param with the Java `key` alias.
ToolParam _workItemId() => _idParam('The work item ID');

ToolParam _req(String name, String description,
        {List<String> aliases = const [], String type = 'string'}) =>
    ToolParam(
      name: name,
      description: description,
      aliases: aliases,
      type: type,
    );

ToolDefinition _opTool(
  String name,
  String description,
  List<ToolParam> params, {
  List<String> aliases = const [],
}) =>
    ToolDefinition(
      name: name,
      aliases: aliases,
      description: description,
      integration: 'ado',
      category: 'work_item_management',
      params: params,
    );

Actually the ADO documentation: Hierarchy link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy`: Forward end name = "Child", Reverse end name = "Parent". When you add a link to work item A with link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` and URL of B, then B becomes... The forward link means A → B in forward direction, so B is the child of A? Let me recall: For tree queries, Parent link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Reverse` (pointing to parent), Child link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` (pointing to child). So if item A has a link of type Hierarchy-Forward to B, then B is A's child, i.e., A is the parent.

/// Tracker-agnostic ADO ticket-operation tools (dm.ai #661/#663 parity):
/// definitions and executor handlers. Names, params, aliases and
/// descriptions mirror the Java `@MCPTool` annotations.
part of 'ado_tools.dart';

/// Id param with the Java `key` alias.
ToolParam _workItemId() => _idParam('The work item ID');

ToolParam _req(String name, String description,
        {List<String> aliases = const [], String type = 'string'}) =>
    ToolParam(
      name: name,
      description: description,
      aliases: aliases,
      type: type,
    );

ToolDefinition _opTool(
  String name,
  String description,
  List<ToolParam> params, {
  List<String> aliases = const [],
}) =>
    ToolDefinition(
      name: name,
      aliases: aliases,
      description: description,
      integration: 'ado',
      category: 'work_item_management',
      params: params,
    );

/// `ado_create_work_item` — Java `createWorkItemWithFieldsJson`.
ToolDefinition _createWorkItemTool() => _opTool(
      'ado_create_work_item',
      'Create a new work item in Azure DevOps',
      [
        _req('project', 'The project name'),
        _req('workItemType', 'The work item type (Bug, Task, User Story, etc.)',
            aliases: ['issueType', 'type']),
        _req('title', 'The work item title', aliases: ['summary']),
        ToolParam(
          name: 'description',
          description: 'The work item description (HTML)',
          required: false,
        ),
        ToolParam(
          name: 'fieldsJson',
          description: 'Additional fields as JSON object (e.g., '
              '{"Microsoft.VSTS.Common.Priority": 1})',
          required: false,
          type: 'object',
        ),
        ToolParam(
          name: 'parentId',
          description: 'Optional parent work item ID: the new item is '
              'created as its child (Hierarchy link)',
          required: false,
          aliases: ['parentKey'],
        ),
      ],
      aliases: ['tracker_create_ticket'],
    );

/// Ticket-operation tools added for dm.ai #661.
List<ToolDefinition> _ticketOpTools() => [
      _opTool('ado_move_to_state', 'Move a work item to a specific state', [
        _workItemId(),
        _req('state', 'The target state name', aliases: ['statusName']),
      ], aliases: [
        'tracker_move_to_status'
      ]),
      _opTool('ado_assign_work_item', 'Assign a work item to a user', [
        _workItemId(),
        _req('userEmail', 'The user email or display name',
            aliases: ['accountId']),
      ], aliases: [
        'tracker_assign_ticket',
        'tracker_assign'
      ]),
      _opTool(
          'ado_update_description', 'Update the description of a work item', [
        _workItemId(),
        _req('description', 'The new description (HTML format)'),
      ],
          aliases: [
            'tracker_update_description'
          ]),
      _opTool(
        'ado_update_tags',
        'Update the tags of a work item (semicolon-separated string)',
        [
          _workItemId(),
          _req(
              'tags',
              "Tags as semicolon-separated string (e.g., "
                  "'tag1;tag2;tag3')"),
        ],
      ),
      ..._ticketFieldTools(),
      ..._ticketLinkTools(),
    ];

/// Field-level tools: update-field, set-priority, get-field-code.
List<ToolDefinition> _ticketFieldTools() => [
      _opTool(
          'ado_update_field',
          'Update any field of a work item. The field may be a reference '
              'name (System.Title, Custom.SolutionDesign) or a common human '
              'name (summary, title, description, priority, tags, state, '
              'assignedTo, storyPoints), which is mapped to its reference '
              'name. Unknown names are passed through unchanged.',
          [
            _workItemId(),
            _req('field', 'Field reference name or common name'),
            _req('value', 'The new value'),
          ],
          aliases: [
            'tracker_update_field'
          ]),
      _opTool(
          'ado_set_priority',
          'Set the priority of a work item. Accepts the ADO numbers 1-4 or '
              'Jira-style names (Blocker/Highest/Critical=1, High/Major=2, '
              'Medium/Normal=3, Low/Minor/Lowest/Trivial=4).',
          [
            _workItemId(),
            _req('priority', 'Priority number 1-4 or a priority name'),
          ],
          aliases: [
            'tracker_set_priority'
          ]),
      _opTool(
          'ado_get_field_code',
          'Resolve a human-readable field name to its reference name for the '
              "project (the analogue of jira_get_field_custom_code). Returns "
              "e.g. 'Custom.SolutionDesign' or 'System.Title'; returns null "
              'when no field with that name exists.',
          [
            ToolParam(
              name: 'project',
              description: 'The project name (defaults to the configured '
                  'project)',
              required: false,
            ),
            _req(
                'fieldName',
                "The human-readable field name (e.g. 'Solution Design') or "
                    'reference name'),
          ],
          aliases: [
            'tracker_get_field_code'
          ]),
    ];

/// Tracker-agnostic ADO ticket-operation tools (dm.ai #661/#663 parity):
/// definitions and executor handlers. Names, params, aliases and
/// descriptions mirror the Java `@MCPTool` annotations.
part of 'ado_tools.dart';

/// Id param with the Java `key` alias.
ToolParam _workItemId() => _idParam('The work item ID');

ToolParam _req(String name, String description,
        {List<String> aliases = const [], String type = 'string'}) =>
    ToolParam(
      name: name,
      description: description,
      aliases: aliases,
      type: type,
    );

ToolDefinition _opTool(
  String name,
  String description,
  List<ToolParam> params, {
  List<String> aliases = const [],
}) =>
    ToolDefinition(
      name: name,
      aliases: aliases,
      description: description,
      integration: 'ado',
      category: 'work_item_management',
      params: params,
    );

/// `ado_create_work_item` — Java `createWorkItemWithFieldsJson`.
ToolDefinition _createWorkItemTool() => _opTool(
      'ado_create_work_item',
      'Create a new work item in Azure DevOps',
      [
        _req('project', 'The project name'),
        _req('workItemType', 'The work item type (Bug, Task, User Story, etc.)',
            aliases: ['issueType', 'type']),
        _req('title', 'The work item title', aliases: ['summary']),
        ToolParam(
          name: 'description',
          description: 'The work item description (HTML)',
          required: false,
        ),
        ToolParam(
          name: 'fieldsJson',
          description: 'Additional fields as JSON object (e.g., '
              '{"Microsoft.VSTS.Common.Priority": 1})',
          required: false,
          type: 'object',
        ),
        ToolParam(
          name: 'parentId',
          description: 'Optional parent work item ID: the new item is '
              'created as its child (Hierarchy link)',
          required: false,
          aliases: ['parentKey'],
        ),
      ],
      aliases: ['tracker_create_ticket'],
    );

/// Ticket-operation tools added for dm.ai #661.
List<ToolDefinition> _ticketOpTools() => [
      _opTool('ado_move_to_state', 'Move a work item to a specific state', [
        _workItemId(),
        _req('state', 'The target state name', aliases: ['statusName']),
      ], aliases: [
        'tracker_move_to_status'
      ]),
      _opTool('ado_assign_work_item', 'Assign a work item to a user', [
        _workItemId(),
        _req('userEmail', 'The user email or display name',
            aliases: ['accountId']),
      ], aliases: [
        'tracker_assign_ticket',
        'tracker_assign'
      ]),
      _opTool(
          'ado_update_description', 'Update the description of a work item', [
        _workItemId(),
        _req('description', 'The new description (HTML format)'),
      ],
          aliases: [
            'tracker_update_description'
          ]),
      _opTool(
        'ado_update_tags',
        'Update the tags of a work item (semicolon-separated string)',
        [
          _workItemId(),
          _req(
              'tags',
              "Tags as semicolon-separated string (e.g., "
                  "'tag1;tag2;tag3')"),
        ],
      ),
      ..._ticketFieldTools(),
      ..._ticketLinkTools(),
    ];

/// Field-level tools: update-field, set-priority, get-field-code.
List<ToolDefinition> _ticketFieldTools() => [
      _opTool(
          'ado_update_field',
          'Update any field of a work item. The field may be a reference '
              'name (System.Title, Custom.SolutionDesign) or a common human '
              'name (summary, title, description, priority, tags, state, '
              'assignedTo, storyPoints), which is mapped to its reference '
              'name. Unknown names are passed through unchanged.',
          [
            _workItemId(),
            _req('field', 'Field reference name or common name'),
            _req('value', 'The new value'),
          ],
          aliases: [
            'tracker_update_field'
          ]),
      _opTool(
          'ado_set_priority',
          'Set the priority of a work item. Accepts the ADO numbers 1-4 or '
              'Jira-style names (Blocker/Highest/Critical=1, High/Major=2, '
              'Medium/Normal=3, Low/Minor/Lowest/Trivial=4).',
          [
            _workItemId(),
            _req('priority', 'Priority number 1-4 or a priority name'),
          ],
          aliases: [
            'tracker_set_priority'
          ]),
      _opTool(
          'ado_get_field_code',
          'Resolve a human-readable field name to its reference name for the '
              "project (the analogue of jira_get_field_custom_code). Returns "
              "e.g. 'Custom.SolutionDesign' or 'System.Title'; returns null "
              'when no field with that name exists.',
          [
            ToolParam(
              name: 'project',
              description: 'The project name (defaults to the configured '
                  'project)',
              required: false,
            ),
            _req(
                'fieldName',
                "The human-readable field name (e.g. 'Solution Design') or "
                    'reference name'),
          ],
          aliases: [
            'tracker_get_field_code'
          ]),
    ];

/// Link and attachment tools.

Actually the ADO documentation: Hierarchy link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy`: Forward end name = "Child", Reverse end name = "Parent". When you add a link to work item A with link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` and URL of B, then B becomes... The forward link means A → B in forward direction, so B is the child of A? Let me recall: For tree queries, Parent link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Reverse` (pointing to parent), Child link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` (pointing to child). So if item A has a link of type Hierarchy-Forward to B, then B is A's child, i.e., A is the parent.

Java createWorkItemWithFieldsJson: `String.format("/%s/_apis/wit/workitems/$%s", projectName, workItemType)` — no explicit encoding in Java either (OkHttp encodes implicitly per the commit message). Dart async relies on Uri.parse, sync encodes explicitly. OK.

Java `ado_create_work_item` declares aliases `{"issueType"}` only for workItemType — wait: `aliases = {"issueType"}`. The Dart adds `aliases: ['issueType', 'type']` — 'type' extra for backward compat with the old Dart tool param named `type`. Good — documented? It's a deliberate superset for backward compatibility. OK.

Now the attach file Java code:
{"command":"sed -n '1040,1130p' /tmp/AzureDevOpsClient.java"}

Java `attachFileToTicket` accepts `contentType` and uses it for the media type (`MediaType.parse(contentType != null && !contentType.isEmpty() ? contentType : "application/octet-stream")`) — although interestingly the `.header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")` is hardcoded and RequestBody uses `MediaType.parse("application/octet-stream")` too... Look carefully:

```java
MediaType mediaType = MediaType.parse(contentType != null && !contentType.isEmpty()
        ? contentType : "application/octet-stream");
...
.post(RequestBody.create(file, MediaType.parse("application/octet-stream")))
```

The computed `mediaType` is... actually NOT used! The upload request uses `.header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")` and `RequestBody.create(file, MediaType.parse("application/octet-stream"))`. So `mediaType` is computed but unused in Java too (dead variable — Java bug carried over). Hmm wait, let me re-read. `.header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")` — hardcoded. `RequestBody.create(file, MediaType.parse("application/octet-stream"))` — hardcoded. So the Java `contentType` param is effectively ignored too (the mediaType variable is dead). Interesting! So the Dart port hardcoding octet-stream actually MATCHES Java's effective behavior. The `mediaType` variable in Java is dead code.

So my "contentType ignored" finding downgrades: Java declares the param and (nominally) computes mediaType, but the effective request is always octet-stream in both. The Dart tool declares `contentType` param and ignores it — same as Java's effective behavior. So it's at most a SUGGESTION (dead param declared in schema; could either honor it or document it as accepted-for-parity). Actually, since the fixture `java_mcp_tool_params.txt` requires the param to exist for parity, and Java's behavior also ignores it, the Dart code matching this is fine. I'll make it a SUGGESTION with a note that both Java and Dart effectively ignore it — maybe honoring contentType would be a small improvement (pass to uploadAttachment). Not blocking.

Now the Java link for parent: comment says "source = parent, target = child -> 'parent' relationship (Hierarchy-Reverse), see mapRelationshipType" — but the CODE calls `linkIssueWithRelationship(parentId.trim(), createdId, "child")`. With relationship "child": mapRelationshipType("child") = Hierarchy-Forward, and the link is created on the source (parentId) pointing to target (createdId) with Hierarchy-Forward. Hierarchy-Forward on the parent = "child" relations of parent. So effective: parent gets a Hierarchy-Forward link to child. The Java COMMENT is wrong/misleading but code is: parent → child Hierarchy-Forward. The Dart does the same: `linkWorkItems(parentId, childId, 'child')` → patch on parentId with Hierarchy-Forward url → child. Matches Java behavior. Good. (The Dart doc comment on createWorkItem says "links it as the parent's child (Hierarchy-Forward on the parent)" — correct.)

Actually the ADO documentation: Hierarchy link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy`: Forward end name = "Child", Reverse end name = "Parent". When you add a link to work item A with link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` and URL of B, then B becomes... The forward link means A → B in forward direction, so B is the child of A? Let me recall: For tree queries, Parent link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Reverse` (pointing to parent), Child link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` (pointing to child). So if item A has a link of type Hierarchy-Forward to B, then B is A's child, i.e., A is the parent.

Actually the ADO documentation: Hierarchy link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy`: Forward end name = "Child", Reverse end name = "Parent". When you add a link to work item A with link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` and URL of B, then B becomes... The forward link means A → B in forward direction, so B is the child of A? Let me recall: For tree queries, Parent link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Reverse` (pointing to parent), Child link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` (pointing to child). So if item A has a link of type Hierarchy-Forward to B, then B is A's child, i.e., A is the parent.

Interesting — Java's doc comment at 790: "Hierarchy-Forward: source is child, target is parent (child → parent); Hierarchy-Reverse: source is parent, target is child (parent → child)". Wait, that contradicts what I said. Let me think about ADO semantics:

In ADO:
- `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` means: this link points FORWARD to the "child" end... Actually in ADO work item linking, the link type has ReferenceName `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` — when you add a link with Hierarchy-Forward from item A to item B, A is the PARENT? No wait.

ADO docs: Link types:
- `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` — "Child" (the forward name is "Child"): source is parent, target is child? Hmm.

Actually the ADO documentation: Hierarchy link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy`: Forward end name = "Child", Reverse end name = "Parent". When you add a link to work item A with link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` and URL of B, then B becomes... The forward link means A → B in forward direction, so B is the child of A? Let me recall: For tree queries, Parent link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Reverse` (pointing to parent), Child link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` (pointing to child). So if item A has a link of type Hierarchy-Forward to B, then B is A's child, i.e., A is the parent.

Java: parent link on creation: `linkIssueWithRelationship(parentId, createdId, "child")` — source = parentId, mapRelationshipType("child") = Hierarchy-Forward, patch applied to source (parentId) with url → createdId. Actually the ADO documentation: Hierarchy link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy`: Forward end name = "Child", Reverse end name = "Parent". When you add a link to work item A with link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` and URL of B, then B becomes... The forward link means A → B in forward direction, so B is the child of A? Let me recall: For tree queries, Parent link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Reverse` (pointing to parent), Child link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` (pointing to child). So if item A has a link of type Hierarchy-Forward to B, then B is A's child, i.e., A is the parent.

Hmm wait, let me re-read. `.header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")` — hardcoded. `RequestBody.create(file, MediaType.parse("application/octet-stream"))` — hardcoded. Interesting — Java's doc comment at 790: "Hierarchy-Forward: source is child, target is parent (child → parent); Hierarchy-Reverse: source is parent, target is child (parent → child)". Wait, that contradicts what I said. Let me think about ADO semantics:

In ADO:
- `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` means: this link points FORWARD to the "child" end... Actually in ADO work item linking, the link type has ReferenceName `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` — when you add a link with Hierarchy-Forward from item A to item B, A is the PARENT? No wait.

ADO docs: Link types:
- `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` — "Child" (the forward name is "Child"): source is parent, target is child? Hmm.

Actually the ADO documentation: Hierarchy link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy`: Forward end name = "Child", Reverse end name = "Parent". When you add a link to work item A with link type `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` and URL of B, then B becomes... The forward link means A → B in forward direction, so B is the child of A? Let me recall: For tree queries, Parent link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Reverse` (pointing to parent), Child link is `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` (pointing to child). So if item A has a link of type Hierarchy-Forward to B, then B is A's child, i.e., A is the parent.

Java: parent link on creation: `linkIssueWithRelationship(parentId, createdId, "child")` — source = parentId, mapRelationshipType("child") = Hierarchy-Forward, patch applied to source (parentId) with url → createdId. So parent item gets Hierarchy-Forward link to child → child is child of parent. Correct.

The Java doc comment at 790 ("Hierarchy-Forward: source is child, target is parent") is actually WRONG relative to ADO semantics (or relative to their own usage), but the mapping "child" → Hierarchy-Forward and patch-on-source makes the behavior right: parent gets forward link to child. Dart matches the code behavior (patch on parentId with Hierarchy-Forward url = child id). Good — Dart is behaviorally consistent with Java. The Dart doc says "links it as the parent's child (Hierarchy-Forward on the parent)" — correct.

Also Java `linkIssueWithRelationship` target URL: `basePath + "/_apis/wit/workItems/" + targetId` — basePath is `{base}/{org}`? In Java client, `path(path)` prepends `/{project}`? They use `basePath + "/_apis/wit/workItems/"`. Java `basePath` presumably = `{base}/{org}`. Dart sync `_orgUrl(c)` = baseUrl minus '/_apis' minus project → `{base}/{org}`, then adds `/_apis/wit/workItems/$target`. Dart async uses `_http.buildOrgUrl('wit/workItems/$targetId')` = `{base}/{org}/_apis/wit/workItems/{id}`. Match.

One subtle diff: Java's target URL is NOT encoded/validated; Dart same. OK.

Now `resolveFieldName` Java 212: contains('.') → as-is; else switch on lowercase name. The Dart `_fieldNames` table should match. Let me verify the Java table.
{"command":"sed -n '204,260p' /tmp/AzureDevOpsClient.java; echo ====; sed -n '617,660p' /tmp/AzureDevOpsClient.java"}

In other calls they do `path(String.format("/%s/_apis/wit/workitems/%s", project, ...))` — so `path()` is the helper that prepends basePath + project?? Wait, if `path()` prepends the project, then `"/%s/_apis/wit/fields"` with target would double the project? Let me check the `path` helper in BasicAzureDevOpsClient or AbstractRestClient. Actually in the create method: `String path = String.format("/%s/_apis/wit/workitems/$%s", projectName, workItemType); GenericRequest request = new GenericRequest(this, path(path))`. So `path(...)` takes the full project-scoped path. The Dart `getInProject(project, 'wit/fields')` builds `{base}/{org}/{project}/_apis/wit/fields`. Equivalent. OK.

Now the Java getFieldCode when project empty: `String target = (projectName != null && !projectName.trim().isEmpty()) ? projectName.trim() : project;` — uses configured project. Dart async: `project == null || project.trim().isEmpty ? await _http.get('wit/fields') : getInProject(project.trim(), ...)` — `get` uses configured project. Match.

Wait — one subtle difference: Java uses `projectName.trim()` for the comparison but then passes `target` (trimmed) into the path; the untrimmed `projectName` never hits the URL. Dart async passes `project.trim()`. Match. Sync: `Uri.encodeComponent(project)` — NOT trimmed! `adoArg(a, ['project']).trim()` — sync does trim. OK.

Now — Java's moveToStatus has param `id` with alias `key`; Dart `_workItemId()` = `_idParam('The work item ID')` — check `_idParam` has alias `key`. Let me check ado_tools.dart _idParam definition.

Java updateDescription: id alias `key`. Dart `_workItemId()` — need to check.

Java updateTags: id WITHOUT alias key in Java! (`@MCPParam(name = "id", description = "The work item ID", required = true)` — no aliases). Dart `ado_update_tags` uses `_workItemId()` which has the key alias. Minor superset — harmless.

Java attachFile: id aliases {"ticketKey", "key"} — Dart `_req('id', ..., aliases: ['ticketKey', 'key'], type: 'number')` — wait, Java id is String; Dart declares type 'number'. Hmm — `ado_attach_file` in Dart: `_req('id', 'The work item ID', aliases: ['ticketKey', 'key'], type: 'number')`. The java_mcp_tool_params fixture only tracks param names, not types. The declared type 'number' vs Java String — the handler `_id(a)` probably coerces. Minor.

Now the key drift check — `java_mcp_param_drift.txt` removed two lines:
- `ado_add_work_item_comment:id,comment` — Java now has id,comment; Dart before had id,text → drift resolved by renaming to comment + alias text.
- `ado_create_work_item:project,workItemType,title,description,fieldsJson` — Java now has parentId too; Dart now declares all 6.

Java `attachFileToTicket` accepts `contentType` and uses it for the media type (`MediaType.parse(contentType != null && !contentType.isEmpty() ? contentType : "application/octet-stream")`) — although interestingly the `.header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")` is hardcoded and RequestBody uses `MediaType.parse("application/octet-stream")` too... Look carefully:

```java
MediaType mediaType = MediaType.parse(contentType != null && !contentType.isEmpty()
        ? contentType : "application/octet-stream");
...
.post(RequestBody.create(file, MediaType.parse("application/octet-stream")))
```

The computed `mediaType` is... actually NOT used! The upload request uses `.header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")` and `RequestBody.create(file, MediaType.parse("application/octet-stream"))`. So `mediaType` is computed but unused in Java too (dead variable — Java bug carried over). Hmm wait, let me re-read. `.header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")` — hardcoded. `RequestBody.create(file, MediaType.parse("application/octet-stream"))` — hardcoded. So the Java `contentType` param is effectively ignored too (the mediaType variable is dead). Interesting! So the Dart port hardcoding octet-stream actually MATCHES Java's effective behavior. The `mediaType` variable in Java is dead code.

So my "contentType ignored" finding downgrades: Java declares the param and (nominally) computes mediaType, but the effective request is always octet-stream in both. The Dart tool declares `contentType` param and ignores it — same as Java's effective behavior. So it's at most a SUGGESTION (dead param declared in schema; could either honor it or document it as accepted-for-parity). Actually, since the fixture `java_mcp_tool_params.txt` requires the param to exist for parity, and Java's behavior also ignores it, the Dart code matching this is fine. I'll make it a SUGGESTION with a note that both Java and Dart effectively ignore it — maybe honoring contentType would be a small improvement (pass to uploadAttachment). Not blocking.

Now the Java link for parent: comment says "source = parent, target = child -> 'parent' relationship (Hierarchy-Reverse), see mapRelationshipType" — but the CODE calls `linkIssueWithRelationship(parentId.trim(), createdId, "child")`. With relationship "child": mapRelationshipType("child") = Hierarchy-Forward, and the link is created on the source (parentId) pointing to target (createdId) with Hierarchy-Forward. Hierarchy-Forward on the parent = "child" relations of parent. So effective: parent gets a Hierarchy-Forward link to child. The Java COMMENT is wrong/misleading but code is: parent → child Hierarchy-Forward. The Dart does the same: `linkWorkItems(parentId, childId, 'child')` → patch on parentId with Hierarchy-Forward url → child. Matches Java behavior. Good. 💡 **SUGGESTION: `contentType` param is declared but silently ignored**

The tool schema advertises `contentType` ("defaults to application/octet-stream", Java parity per `java_mcp_tool_params.txt`), but the handler drops it:

```dart
'ado_attach_file': (a) =>
    ops.attachFile(_id(a), _s(a, 'name'), _s(a, 'filePath')),
```

Behavior parity is therefore preserved; the issue is only that the Dart schema (like Java's) advertises a knob that does nothing.

Options:
- honor it: thread `contentType` through `attachFile` → `uploadAttachment`/`syncCurlUpload` as the request Content-Type (small, genuinely useful for `image/png` uploads), or
- keep as-is for fixture parity but drop the dead `_s`-style reads so it's obvious the param is accepted-for-parity only.

💡 **SUGGESTION: inconsistent alias handling — manual fallback vs `applyParamAliases`**

Tool-bridge dispatch already normalizes aliases before handlers run (`tool_bridge.dart:303` calls `tool.applyParamAliases(args)`, and `workItemType` declares `aliases: ['issueType', 'type']`). 'ado_create_work_item': (a) => ops.createWorkItem(
```dart
      project: _s(a, 'project'),

```

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `contentType` param is declared but silently ignored**

The tool schema advertises `contentType` ("defaults to application/octet-stream", Java parity per `java_mcp_tool_params.txt`), but the handler drops it:

```dart
'ado_attach_file': (a) =>
    ops.attachFile(_id(a), _s(a, 'name'), _s(a, 'filePath')),
```

Both transports then hardcode octet-stream (`uploadAttachment` in `ado_http_client.dart`, `_upload` in `ado_sync_work_item_ops.dart`).

Parity note: upstream Java *effectively* ignores it too — `attachFileToTicket` computes `MediaType mediaType = MediaType.parse(contentType …)` but then posts with a hardcoded `.header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")` and `RequestBody.create(file, MediaType.parse("application/octet-stream"))`, so the computed `mediaType` is dead code there. Behavior parity is therefore preserved; the issue is only that the Dart schema (like Java's) advertises a knob that does nothing.

Options:
- honor it: thread `contentType` through `attachFile` → `uploadAttachment`/`syncCurlUpload` as the request Content-Type (small, genuinely useful for `image/png` uploads), or
- keep as-is for fixture parity but drop the dead `_s`-style reads so it's obvious the param is accepted-for-parity only.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: inconsistent alias handling — manual fallback vs `applyParamAliases`**

Tool-bridge dispatch already normalizes aliases before handlers run (`tool_bridge.dart:303` calls `tool.applyParamAliases(args)`, and `workItemType` declares `aliases: ['issueType', 'type']`). Yet this handler adds a manual fallback for `type` — while sibling params (`title`/`summary`, `state`/`statusName`, `description`) rely on the bridge alone:

```dart
'ado_create_work_item': (a) => ops.createWorkItem(
      project: _s(a, 'project'),
      workItemType: _s(a, 'workItemType', 'type'),  // manual alias here…
      title: _s(a, 'title'),                        // …but not for `summary`
```

The sync executors take a third approach (`adoArg(a, ['userEmail', 'accountId'])` lists), so the alias knowledge now lives in three places: `ToolParam.aliases`, the sync `adoArg` lists, and this one-off `_s(…, alt)` fallback. All three work today, but they will drift — e.g. adding a new alias to the param won't fix a sync `adoArg` list that forgot it.

Suggest picking one layer: either trust `applyParamAliases` and delete the manual fallbacks, or (if the sync handlers must stay self-sufficient because they're also invoked directly in tests) document that the `adoArg` lists are the sync-side mirror of `ToolParam.aliases` and keep the async side bridge-only.

💡 **SUGGESTION: async create path encodes the work-item type only implicitly**

Commit 2111d375 fixed the sync path to `Uri.encodeComponent(type)` because curl rejects a raw space (`User Story` → exit 3). The async path here still interpolates the type raw:

```dart
final body = await _http.postPatch(
  'wit/workitems/\$$workItemType',
  ...
```

This happens to work because dio → `Uri.parse` percent-encodes the space (`%20`) when building the request URI, but that invariant is implicit and easy to break (e.g. anyone switching transport or pre-parsing the URL differently). The sync file carries an explanatory comment for exactly this; the async side has none, and the new async tests only exercise `Task`/`Bug` — the spaced-type case is covered solely by the sync echo-server test.

Suggest:
- add the same one-line comment (or an explicit `Uri.encodeComponent(workItemType)`) here, and
- extend `ado_work_item_ops_test.dart` with a `'User Story'` create asserting the `%20` path, so the async parity of the 2111d375 fix is pinned by a test, not by transport accident.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: inconsistent alias handling — manual fallback vs `applyParamAliases`**

Tool-bridge dispatch already normalizes aliases before handlers run (`tool_bridge.dart:303` calls `tool.applyParamAliases(args)`, and `workItemType` declares `aliases: ['issueType', 'type']`). Yet this handler adds a manual fallback for `type` — while sibling params (`title`/`summary`, `state`/`statusName`, `description`) rely on the bridge alone:

```dart
'ado_create_work_item': (a) => ops.createWorkItem(
      project: _s(a, 'project'),
      workItemType: _s(a, 'workItemType', 'type'),  // manual alias here…
      title: _s(a, 'title'),                        // …but not for `summary`
```

The sync executors take a third approach (`adoArg(a, ['userEmail', 'accountId'])` lists), so the alias knowledge now lives in three places: `ToolParam.aliases`, the sync `adoArg` lists, and this one-off `_s(…, alt)` fallback. All three work today, but they will drift — e.g. adding a new alias to the param won't fix a sync `adoArg` list that forgot it.

Suggest picking one layer: either trust `applyParamAliases` and delete the manual fallbacks, or (if the sync handlers must stay self-sufficient because they're also invoked directly in tests) document that the `adoArg` lists are the sync-side mirror of `ToolParam.aliases` and keep the async side bridge-only.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `contentType` param is declared but silently ignored**

The tool schema advertises `contentType` ("defaults to application/octet-stream", Java parity per `java_mcp_tool_params.txt`), but the handler drops it:

```dart
'ado_attach_file': (a) =>
    ops.attachFile(_id(a), _s(a, 'name'), _s(a, 'filePath')),
```

Both transports then hardcode octet-stream (`uploadAttachment` in `ado_http_client.dart`, `_upload` in `ado_sync_work_item_ops.dart`).

Parity note: upstream Java *effectively* ignores it too — `attachFileToTicket` computes `MediaType mediaType = MediaType.parse(contentType …)` but then posts with a hardcoded `.header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")` and `RequestBody.create(file, MediaType.parse("application/octet-stream"))`, so the computed `mediaType` is dead code there. Behavior parity is therefore preserved; the issue is only that the Dart schema (like Java's) advertises a knob that does nothing.

Options:
- honor it: thread `contentType` through `attachFile` → `uploadAttachment`/`syncCurlUpload` as the request Content-Type (small, genuinely useful for `image/png` uploads), or
- keep as-is for fixture parity but drop the dead `_s`-style reads so it's obvious the param is accepted-for-parity only.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: inconsistent alias handling — manual fallback vs `applyParamAliases`**

Tool-bridge dispatch already normalizes aliases before handlers run (`tool_bridge.dart:303` calls `tool.applyParamAliases(args)`, and `workItemType` declares `aliases: ['issueType', 'type']`). Yet this handler adds a manual fallback for `type` — while sibling params (`title`/`summary`, `state`/`statusName`, `description`) rely on the bridge alone:

```dart
'ado_create_work_item': (a) => ops.createWorkItem(
      project: _s(a, 'project'),
      workItemType: _s(a, 'workItemType', 'type'),  // manual alias here…
      title: _s(a, 'title'),                        // …but not for `summary`
```

The sync executors take a third approach (`adoArg(a, ['userEmail', 'accountId'])` lists), so the alias knowledge now lives in three places: `ToolParam.aliases`, the sync `adoArg` lists, and this one-off `_s(…, alt)` fallback. All three work today, but they will drift — e.g. adding a new alias to the param won't fix a sync `adoArg` list that forgot it.

Suggest picking one layer: either trust `applyParamAliases` and delete the manual fallbacks, or (if the sync handlers must stay self-sufficient because they're also invoked directly in tests) document that the `adoArg` lists are the sync-side mirror of `ToolParam.aliases` and keep the async side bridge-only.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: async create path encodes the work-item type only implicitly**

Commit 2111d375 fixed the sync path to `Uri.encodeComponent(type)` because curl rejects a raw space (`User Story` → exit 3). The async path here still interpolates the type raw:

```dart
final body = await _http.postPatch(
  'wit/workitems/\$$workItemType',
  ...
```

This happens to work because dio → `Uri.parse` percent-encodes the space (`%20`) when building the request URI, but that invariant is implicit and easy to break (e.g. anyone switching transport or pre-parsing the URL differently). The sync file carries an explanatory comment for exactly this; the async side has none, and the new async tests only exercise `Task`/`Bug` — the spaced-type case is covered solely by the sync echo-server test.

Suggest:
- add the same one-line comment (or an explicit `Uri.encodeComponent(workItemType)`) here, and
- extend `ado_work_item_ops_test.dart` with a `'User Story'` create asserting the `%20` path, so the async parity of the 2111d375 fix is pinned by a test, not by transport accident.
